children: Xiaomi Corporation Class B (HKEX:1810) is balancing product momentum—early adoption of Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 chips and a 13.2mm 10,000mAh magnetic power bank—with weakening smartphone shipments (down 30% YoY) and margin pressure from memory costs; the stock, near HK$25.60, has seen buybacks but remains well below its peak.
Xiaomi Class B Slips Market Share
: Xiaomi Class B (1810): Q3 smartphone shipments fell over 30% YoY to about 10% market share after exiting low‑end markets. Margin hit by sharply higher memory costs; Q2 shipments were 31.2M.
: Xiaomi Class B (1810) repurchased 4.4M Type B shares in October: 2.5M for HK$61.2M on Oct 12 and 1.9M for HK$50.8M on Oct 16, totaling HK$112.0M.
: Xiaomi Class B (1810) trading near HK$25.60, about 58% below its peak. Technicals: 50-week below 200-week (death cross), under 61.8% Fibonacci; key support near $19.65 at 78.6% retracement.
Xiaomi Class B Flags Flagship Chips
: Xiaomi Class B (1810) showcased phones with Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 at Snapdragon Summit 2026, signaling early adoption of flagship chipsets for its devices.
: Xiaomi Class B (1810) launched a 13.2mm Jinshajiang 10,000mAh magnetic power bank in China at 399 yuan. Specs: 45W USB-C PD wired, 20W magnetic wireless, silicone-carbon cell; passed safety tests.
